_comment: Study prompt set. 30 neutral category questions, none of which names a
brand except the three deliberate comparison prompts.
Why this differs from the monitor set: 17 of the 35 monitoring prompts
named Flatiron, which guarantees a Flatiron mention and makes any
cross-brand comparison meaningless. A category study has to ask what a
real prospective student would ask before they know which brands exist.
Sourcing: themes were drawn from Blind and Reddit threads about coding
bootcamps, plus the question sets that Course Report, NerdWallet and
Educative publish as their own FAQ sections. The recurring real-world
themes are: is it worth it now, what about AI writing code, job
placement honesty, cost and financing, career change from non-tech,
online vs in person, job guarantees, and apprenticeships as an
BEFORE THE RUN: read these out loud and cut any that sound like a
marketer wrote them. The study's credibility rests on these being
Intents: informational | commercial | comparative | navigational | transactional
